content: #1 of 3 in Lorsch. The Lorsch Abbey ( _St. Nazarius_ ) was a Benedictine abbey in Lorsch in the southern Hessian district Bergstraße in Germany. In 1232 the monastery came to the archbishopric of Mainz and was pledged in 1461 to the Palatinate, which abolished the monastery in 1564. The monastery was founded, according to the Lorsch Codex, as a noble monastery of the Robertiner Cancor (Count in Alemannien to 758 and until his death in 771 Count in Oberrheingau) and his mother Williswinth on the Weschnitz. This church was probably extended to a monastery for the purpose of the family grave lay and in 764 Bishop Chrodegang of Metz (a relative of Williswinth and Cancor) transferred to personal possession. In the tradition of eternal prayer (in the early days of the monastery for the families of the owners and the wealthy nobility), Charlemagne also called on the monks to pray for the royal family and the kingdom.
